expectedBehavior: Each operation, page, owner, auth, test, DEV, seed, and cleanup path is deterministic.
Approved deployable, owner, dual-app, generated-client, carry-over, and foundation boundaries hold.
blindReviewDeclaration: Independent verdict frozen before author, intake, or Claude material.

findings.title: The 104 operation contracts are not implementation-deterministic
findings.evidence: edge-operation-inventory.md §2 has method/path/face only; edge-contract-dialectical-assessment.md §3 is grouped; development-agent-execution-blueprint.md §3.3 and whole-scope-design.md §2.2/§5.2 give global, not per-operation, rules
findings.risk: Contract divergence can pass global rules.
findings.counterexample: An agent can implement createWorkspace/updateContract with different field names, nullability, transitions, errorCode values, auth negatives, and page bindings while satisfying every global rule.
findings.reason: DTO/field/status/error/page-operation/test details for 104 operations remain implementation choices; a green build can be contract-incompatible.
findings.minimalRepair: Freeze a per-operation matrix for request/response fields, exact errors, transitions, auth/session negatives, page anchor and test ID, bidirectionally bound to scenarios and owner transactions.
findings.largerAlternativeCost: Per-module or per-face review would repeat ceremony and violate atomic R5; one generated matrix is cheaper.

findings.title: The 32 scenario and 104 operation denominators lack a bidirectional crosswalk
findings.evidence: edge-operation-inventory.md §1 counts 32 scenarios/104 operations; whole-scope-implementation-design.md §9 maps scenarios to units only; whole-scope-manifest-chapter-hit-map.md has no literal reverse crosswalk
findings.risk: Missing or extra operations can hide behind totals.
findings.counterexample: An operation can be counted and assigned to a unit without a Journey step invoking it, while a scenario can appear covered with a required operation missing or replaced.
findings.reason: The denominator is counted but not falsifiable in both directions across three consumer faces.
findings.minimalRepair: Add checked scenario-step↔operation ID/path/face/owner/page/capability/disposition rows, including the two deletions and one addition.
findings.largerAlternativeCost: A traceability database or Journey-by-Journey review is unnecessary; checked JSON is smaller.

findings.title: Managed DEV, remote, seed, and cleanup are not one deterministic fixture contract
findings.evidence: development-agent-execution-blueprint.md §12 gives stages but not fixture rows; whole-scope-implementation-design.md §7.1-§7.3 gives obligations without complete stable fixtures/readbacks; granularity manifest U11/U12 binds scripts broadly
findings.risk: Clean runs can yield incompatible facts, evidence, and cleanup.
findings.counterexample: Two clean remote runs can both report r5-full receipts yet choose different namespace, IDs, credentials, asset keys, row counts, idempotency keys, negative fixtures, and cleanup predicates.
findings.reason: Remote readiness, rich seed, bootstrap direct-write allowlist, deterministic fixture identities, per-scenario negatives, and cleanup are not executable as one fixture contract.
findings.minimalRepair: Freeze namespace/connection source, exact keys/counts for all 32 scenarios, credentials/assets, idempotency keys, readbacks, negatives, reset allowlist, and separate business/cleanup PASS predicates.
findings.largerAlternativeCost: A generalized environment platform would add forbidden complexity; a versioned r5-full fixture manifest is enough.

findings.title: The platform-admin operation denominator is internally inconsistent
findings.evidence: edge-operation-inventory.md §1 says platform-admin=38; granularity manifest U08 approvedAssertions says 40-operation platform closure
findings.risk: Generated and acceptance denominators can diverge.
findings.counterexample: A generator can require two nonexistent platform operations or omit two canonical ones while total 104 still matches.
findings.reason: Unit acceptance and generated contract evidence use incompatible denominators.
findings.minimalRepair: Change 40 to 38 and add a face-count sum check to 104.
findings.largerAlternativeCost: Per-screen closures add maintenance; correction plus sum check is sufficient.

findings.title: UI carry-over and foundation consumption are not bound per surface
findings.evidence: frontend-asset-carry-over-first.md §3 requires source/target asset inventory; frontend-foundation-consumption-rule.md requires shared reuse; granularity manifest U08-U10 uses broad feature-folder surfaces
findings.risk: App-local duplication can pass folder-level checks.
findings.counterexample: An agent can rebuild Drawer/overlay/list-context/role-home mechanics locally and still claim the broad app feature was implemented because no asset, target, primitive, generated slice, or focused proof is bound.
findings.reason: Carry-over and foundation rules exist, but the implementation manifest is not per-surface executable or falsifiable.
findings.minimalRepair: Add source path/hash→v2s target→foundation primitive→generated slice→route→focused evidence rows and reject duplicate local mechanics.
findings.largerAlternativeCost: A visual asset registry service is unnecessary; a checked manifest is smaller.

findings.title: The rejected page-guard contract remains ambiguous in implementation units
findings.evidence: edge-contract-dialectical-assessment.md §3 group 18 rejects checkOperationsPageEntryGuard; whole-scope-implementation-design.md U06 says page guard while U09/U10 say navigation guard
findings.risk: A rejected endpoint or second auth truth can return.
findings.counterexample: One agent can expose a new page-guard endpoint and another can use an internal predicate; the design cannot distinguish forbidden API recreation from the intended route check.
findings.reason: The deletion is not propagated to an explicit internal-only authorization rule.
findings.minimalRepair: Name an internal route/navigation check, forbid a page-guard endpoint/read edge, and bind every route to its owner authorization source.
findings.largerAlternativeCost: A policy engine is disproportionate; a negative contract assertion and route table suffice.

findings.title: The R5-U03 approved corpus source anchor is unresolved
findings.evidence: granularity manifest U03 anchor is `## G-03 三类用户必须分开`; current corpus heading is `## G-03 三类用户、总公司与门店关联`; manifest review check returns UNIT_SOURCE_R5-U03_1_ANCHOR_NOT_UNIQUE:0
findings.risk: The U03 source binding is not reproducible.
findings.counterexample: The manifest-plus-review gate cannot prove U03's first source binding although the file hash matches.
findings.reason: A frozen source anchor is not resolvable, so U03 evidence is not mechanically reproducible.
findings.minimalRepair: Refresh the literal anchor to the current heading and rerun the manifest check.
findings.largerAlternativeCost: A new source-registry mechanism is broader than correcting this stale anchor.

solutionReasonableness.problemFit: Scope and architecture fit, but implementation determinism does not.
solutionReasonableness.simplerAlternativeAssessment: Checked operation, trace, UI, route, and fixture matrices are simpler than splitting R5 or adding platforms.
solutionReasonableness.costFit: Bounded design repair is cheaper than transferring ambiguity to implementation and verification.

conclusion.summary: R5 DESIGN is NO_GO: 3 M, 4 S, 0 N; all 12 units reviewed.
conclusion.authorizationBoundary: Design review only; no implementation, DEV, remote, seed, reset, source, or repository authority.
